item.title: Issue #2811 created
item.description:
fn:decode-from-uri: to +, or not to +

We decided that fn:decode-from-uri should turn a plus character into a space, so that a+b.xml is decoded as a b.xml.

That rule actually comes from HTML form data (as I was informed), not from URIs, so the function does not really do what its name promises. It does not match its own counterpart fn:encode-for-uri either, which writes + as %2B. In addition, it seems to break fn:parse-uri, which reuses the same decoding for path segments.

We could add an option to control the behavior for +, but it may be over the top.
